content.title: About
content.content: Chard (Beta vulgaris subsp. cicla) is a leafy vegetable related to beetroot. It is cultivated in temperate regions and prized for its tender stems and large leaf blades. Raw chard has a mildly bitter, nutty flavor and a crisp texture. It is used in salads, smoothies, and as a quick‑cooked side dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chard belongs to the same family as beet, spinach, and Swiss chard varieties.
Historical records show chard cultivation dating back to ancient Rome.
The green stems contain betaine, which can change the color of dishes when heated.
In some countries chard is nicknamed “Swiss mango” because of its bright green‑yellow hue.
Chard grows easily in home containers and pots.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Chard provides a high amount of vitamin K, essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of vitamins A and C
items.content: Vitamins A and C support vision, immunity, and act as antioxidants.

items.title: Contains magnesium and potassium
items.content: These minerals help maintain normal muscle and nerve function and regulate blood pressure.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and supports gut microbiota.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Chard is low in calories, making it a great addition to weight‑management diets.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Chard contains oxalates, which may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: As with many leafy greens, chard can retain pesticide residues; thorough washing is recommended.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Rarely, some people may experience an allergy to chard.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw chard can be added to salads, smoothies, wraps, and sandwiches. Stems are often sliced thinly, while the leafy part is used as greens. For a milder taste, you can briefly blanch the leaves in hot water.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store chard in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, wrapped in a slightly damp paper towel or in a perforated bag. Use within 3–5 days. Discard any leaves that become yellowed, slimy, or develop an off‑odor.
